title: High-resolution machine-learning catalog outlines a potential unmapped fault in the Weiyuan shale-gas region
summary: A machine-learning event detector combined with waveform cross-correlation produced a high-resolution catalog for injection-induced seismicity in the Weiyuan area, identifying one-third more earthquakes than the routine catalog and improving magnitude completeness. Spatial migration patterns show a pore-pressure diffusion front; a cluster outlines a potential unmapped fault that may have hosted the region’s largest recorded event, the September 2019 Mw 5.2 earthquake.
ai_technology: Machine-learning earthquake detector combined with waveform cross-correlation (the abstract does not name a particular detector architecture)
organization: The Chinese University of Hong Kong; Sichuan Earthquake Agency

evidence.tested: A machine-learning event detector combined with waveform cross-correlation produced a high-resolution catalog for injection-induced seismicity in the Weiyuan area, identifying one-third more earthquakes than the routine catalog and improving magnitude completeness.
evidence.unknown: The authors describe the fault as potential and state that it may have led to the September 2019 Mw 5.2 event; this is an interpretation, not a directly imaged fault or established causal proof. Results are from one field area and are limited by the station coverage.
evidence.ai_role: Detected additional earthquakes that enabled higher-resolution relocation and spatiotemporal mapping; authors use the denser catalog to infer a migrating pore-pressure front and identify a cluster outlining a potential fault trace.
